name: Academic
one_line: The fact schema that becomes legal when a file's own evidence shows it was produced or received by studying or teaching a specific course of study: school, term, subject, instructor, work_type.
design_cite: Academic files may use school, term, course, instructor, and work type

fields.why: 00 names it: "Academic files may use school, term, course, instructor, and work type". Ceiling is validated, not direct, because the rule family that confirms it is a schools gazetteer hit matched at a word boundary plus role context that separates the holder's own school from an institution the file is addressed to; 00 forbids the name on its own: "A university name alone should not create a group because Columbia can appear as an authoring school, course provider, target institution, employer, research venue, or merely a cited organization." A school name read out of PDF or DOCX author/producer metadata is not this fact — "PDF metadata should be treated as supporting evidence, not as truth".

00 names it: "Academic files may use school, term, course, instructor, and work type". Rule family: dedicated academic-term patterns, never generic date parsing — "Academic terms such as Spring 2025, AY 2024-25, and Michaelmas Term 2024 require dedicated patterns rather than generic parsing." A filesystem timestamp, a due date, or a calendar DTSTART year is evidence about the file, not a term fact.

00 names it as course — "Academic files may use school, term, course, instructor, and work type" — and D6 (ratified 2026-08-21) makes subject the stored key. Rule family is 00's own pattern-plus-context shape: "BUSIB 4300 becomes a course fact only when the engine finds a course-code pattern together with academic context such as “syllabus,” “lecture,” “credits,” “instructor,” or “semester.”" The context term must describe the document itself, not a list inside it; a course-code token in a resume's coursework enumeration is a low-weight late-body occurrence — "a value in a filename or document title carries more meaning than the same value in a footer or a late body-page reference".

00 names it: "Academic files may use school, term, course, instructor, and work type". Ceiling is direct only from an explicitly labelled slot — a syllabus table row or form field whose label reads Instructor, which is what 00's table extraction preserves: "Tables matter because resumes, forms, applications, invoices, and administrative documents often place their most useful information in cells rather than body paragraphs." From prose, a filename or OCR it stays possible, and no rule family promotes it because no person gazetteer exists in this product's scope. Not destination-eligible, per the canonical row and 00: "It should avoid using authorship or creator identity as a destination dimension." It is a search, explanation and review field.

00 names it: "Academic files may use school, term, course, instructor, and work type", and its members are values, not nodes — 00's tree shows Syllabus, Homework and Lectures as branches under one course, and "The system may create new values when it sees a new course, project, company, university, or event, but it should not invent new fields automatically." Rule family: a work-type vocabulary term in a high-weight zone (filename, title, page-one heading, slide-one title) together with coursework structure or another academic signal. This is the one academic field a sparse file can carry alone: HW 3.pdf can reach work_type and still have no subject.

deterministic: a course-code-shaped token in a high-weight zone (filename, document title, page-one or slide-one heading) co-occurring with one of 00's five academic context terms — syllabus, lecture, credits, instructor, semester — describing the document itself
a dedicated academic-term pattern (Spring 2026, AY 2024-25, Michaelmas Term 2024 shapes) co-occurring with a course-code-shaped token or a coursework work-type term
a work-type vocabulary term in a high-weight zone together with coursework document structure (numbered problems, a grading or reading schedule, a lecture deck's slide sequence)
a schools-gazetteer hit matched at a word boundary together with academic role context (registrar, transcript, course listing, enrollment language) rather than admissions or employment language
a labelled Instructor slot in a table cell or form field on a document already carrying course or term evidence
an ICS SUMMARY or DESCRIPTION field carrying a course-code-shaped token plus academic context, where source_type=calendar contributed only as a file-kind signal
needs_llm: an unlabelled prose document whose only academic signal is topic and register — the model must decide whether it reads as coursework or as an application essay, and return unknown when it cannot cite support
OCR of a photographed or screenshotted assignment page where the course token is present but the surrounding words are not one of the five context terms
an archive whose members mix coursework and application documents, where the question is whether one shared purpose explains the packet or a course does
a syllabus or timetable in a language whose term and course-code vocabulary the deterministic pattern catalogue does not cover
a document that uses a programme or module name in prose instead of a code-shaped token (Introduction to Organic Chemistry, Michaelmas tutorial sheet)
never_alone: a university or school name alone — 00: "A university name alone should not create a group because Columbia can appear as an authoring school, course provider, target institution, employer, research venue, or merely a cited organization."

a bare 4-digit number alone — 00 warns of "numbers that look like years but are course identifiers, version numbers, build numbers, ZIP codes, or other unrelated values", so 4300 is neither a term nor a course on its own
a course-code-shaped token with no academic context describing the document — 00's own adversarial list includes "course-code patterns that are actually ZIP codes or device models"

a course-code-shaped token appearing inside a resume's education or relevant-coursework enumeration: the document is a recruiting artifact, the token sits in a late low-weight zone, and no coursework work_type applies to the file itself
a homework- or assignment-shaped filename alone (HW 3.pdf) as proof of a school, term or course — it may support work_type and nothing more
source_type alone: text_document, presentation, spreadsheet, calendar or archive membership never activates this schema without content evidence
an instructor or person name alone, including a DOCX or PDF author field, which may name a template, a prior editor or a script
a parent folder called School, Classes or Uni alone — folder context is a clue, and 00 requires that existing structure not be silently reinterpreted

grouping_reasons: one course in one term — 00: "A course code alone should not merge different semesters; course packet identity should include a term when it is available."
one assignment across its drafts, joined by the universal version family rather than by any academic fact
one course-material neighbourhood in which sparse files are context-supported members only — 00: "The graph does not automatically copy those missing facts onto sparse files."
one school and term study period, when several courses share the same enrollment evidence

template.why: 00 states this order outright — "An Academic template may define school → term → course → work type" — and gives the reason a parent must come first: "A work type such as Homework 3 is meaningful only after the course is known, and a course code may require the school or term to disambiguate it." instructor is excluded because it is not destination-eligible. This is a recommendation, not a filesystem: 00's own worked example offers course → term → work type and school → course as alternatives the user may pick, and the user can reverse, remove or flatten any level.

collides_with.signal: both sides can be evidenced by one university name and by essay-shaped prose. The discriminating evidence: the applications side needs a target-institution plus admissions-cycle or portal pair; the academic side needs a course-code-plus-context pair, a coursework work type, or registrar or enrollment language naming the holder's own school. Neither may take a bare university name.

a lab report, thesis or figure can be evidenced from either side. The discriminating evidence: research needs a project identifier, lab or venue; academic needs a course code with academic context, a term pattern, or a coursework work type. A course-numbered thesis legitimately clears both on disjoint evidence, which is why this pair also carries also_holds_with.

a resume or recruiting document carries the applicant's own school and a graduation term and may list course codes in an education section. The discriminating evidence: the academic side needs the academic context term to describe the document itself, in a high-weight zone, not to appear inside a late enumeration; a document whose own structure is a resume takes neither subject nor work_type.

also_holds_with.signal: one file may legally carry both schemas on disjoint evidence: a transcript keeps school and work_type while the packet supplies purpose and target_university. 00 lists exactly this packet: "an ID, transcript, resume, personal statement, award certificate, and portal screenshot may be content-incoherent but purpose-coherent as an application submission", and "A file may validly belong to more than one accepted group".

a course-numbered thesis, senior project or lab report carries subject and work_type from its course evidence and project, lab or artifact_type from its own research evidence. 00's own two-schema case is the neighbouring one: "An academic abstract submitted as part of a university application can retain project = PVA/RDP and document type = abstract while also carrying purpose = university application and target university = UChicago."

a photographed page of coursework activates photos from camera EXIF and academic from the OCR text — disjoint evidence, two fact sets, no merge. 00: "Hw 5.pdf may be a photographed homework page with no usable text layer".

a transcript, course-completion certificate or professional-certification record carries school, term and work_type from its own academic evidence while serving a recruiting process — the same disjoint-evidence shape as the applications packet. Career is a field-less placeholder schema (PR-6), so this asserts co-activation, not a field overlap. Authored to reciprocate the edge the career node states toward academic.

role_split.why: same entity type, different role: the institution the holder attends versus the institution an application is addressed to. 00: "It should avoid using authorship or creator identity as a destination dimension" is the neighbouring rule; the role separation itself is 00's distinct-facets sentence, and the canonical field list already records the pair.

sensitivity_why: 00 counts this material in the personal corpus it protects: the product "processes a highly personal corpus that can include identity documents, account statements, tax records, medical information, legal records, credentials, private correspondence, GPS metadata, employment materials, and educational records." Transcripts, gradebooks and graded work carry grades, and teaching-side files carry other people's names. Which handling class applies is P7's and is not set here.
open_question: Does potentially_sensitive attach to the whole Academic domain, or only to its grade-bearing and other-people-bearing work types (transcript, gradebook, graded work, class rosters)? Marking the whole domain would gate ordinary coursework out of cloud dossiers; marking only some work types makes sensitivity depend on a fact that is itself only validated. Joseph's call, not this node's.
